clue.text: Robinson Crusoe found a track

parts.note: to found metal is to cast it in a mould
a track or path is a way

explanation.surface: A remark that Defoe's hero discovered a path across his island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' looks like the past of 'find', but here it is the metalworking verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe's hero was shipwrecked and marooned alone on an island, the classic example of someone washed ashore.

clue.text: Firm support required for office equipment

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
a pier is a supporting pillar

explanation.surface: A business needs backing to acquire a photocopying machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A photocopying machine is standard office kit.

clue.text: Lamentably secretive about foreign money

indicators.note: about means placed around, so secretive goes round the money

parts.note: sly means furtive or secretive
the ore is a Scandinavian coin

explanation.surface: Sadly, a furtive person is dealing in overseas currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Grievously or badly, as in sorely missed.

clue.text: A legal right for the non-British

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A legal entitlement granted to people who are not British.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreigner, someone who is not a citizen of the country.

clue.text: A scholar having a certain zest is highly unusual!

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts, a scholar
zing is liveliness or zest

explanation.surface: An academic with genuine verve is a rare find.
explanation.definitionFit: Astonishing or remarkable, out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Claim maybe a quarter-there's vindictiveness!

indicators.note: maybe suggests the word Claim could be rearranged into another form

parts.note: east is one of the four quarters of the compass, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: Someone stakes a claim to a quarter share, and resentment follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarter' suggests a fraction of the claim, but it means a compass point; 'maybe' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Spite or a desire to harm others is what both words describe.

clue.text: One staple product coming from animals

indicators.note: a product is something made, here from the letters of One staple

explanation.surface: A single essential commodity is derived from livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Deer-like grazing mammals of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Thought to tip the perfectionist

parts.note: an idea is a thought
to list is to tip or lean over, as a ship does

explanation.surface: Advice about recommending a fussy person for a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pursuing high principles or perfect standards.

clue.text: Appeal of item about tea-making

indicators.note: about places the item around the other piece

parts.note: an entry is an item in a list

indicators.note: making indicates the word tea is formed afresh from its letters

explanation.surface: A request concerning how to brew a cuppa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tea-making' reads as brewing, but 'making' is the anagram signal working on the drink alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest request or plea.

clue.text: Quiet craftsman, though prejudiced

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical direction for quietly
an artisan is a skilled manual worker

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken workman who nevertheless holds biased views.
explanation.definitionFit: A biased supporter of one side is someone who takes sides unfairly.

clue.text: The way a little citrus tree tends to grow big

indicators.note: only a little of the words citrus tree tends is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A gardening remark about how a small lemon tree tends to grow large.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to grow big' is surface padding joining the definition to the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: A road in a town is a common way or thoroughfare.

clue.text: River responsible for erosion

definitions.meaning: a river in north-east England flowing through Durham and Sunderland
gradual damage by use or friction

explanation.definitionFit: A north-east English waterway, and gradual damage by friction.

clue.text: The wild rose for example can line a minor road

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: to line something is to sit inside it, so the can goes within the road

parts.note: a lane is a narrow country road
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: A hedgerow scene in which wild roses border a country lane.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetbriar is a species of wild rose with fragrant leaves.

clue.text: A story absorbing novices in the city

indicators.note: absorbing means taking something in, so the story holds the novices

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
L is the learner plate, so two learners give LL

explanation.surface: A tale that draws beginners into the life of a town.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in northern France near the Belgian border.

clue.text: Procure a key, being fly

parts.note: to win something is to obtain or procure it
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: Advice on getting hold of a key while being sharp about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly is to travel through the air, as a bird does on the wing.

clue.text: Not willingly late

parts.note: late as in deceased, and not willingly as in having left no will

explanation.definitionFit: Dying without having made a will.

clue.text: Some serving men, work over, take a rest lay up

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a body of soldiers

indicators.note: over signals that the word for work is turned back to front

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
to sit is to take a rest

explanation.surface: Soldiers, their job finished, take a break and put their feet up.
explanation.definitionFit: To deposit or store goods away for later use is to lay them up.

clue.text: Ludicrous outfit, almost all obtained for a song

parts.note: mad means absurd or ludicrous
a rig is a set of clothes

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of all is dropped

explanation.surface: An absurd costume was acquired cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a song' means cheaply on the surface, but 'song' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A part-song for several unaccompanied voices, popular in the Renaissance.

clue.text: Seaman's plot-there's nothing concrete

definitions.note: a phrase standing for an adjective meaning not concrete

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, so his gives ABS
a tract is a plot of land

explanation.surface: A sailor's piece of land turns out to be insubstantial.
explanation.definitionFit: Theoretical rather than physical or tangible.

clue.text: Individual judging a part about right with little hesitation

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the part goes round the right

parts.note: a bit is a part
er is a short hesitant sound

explanation.surface: Someone weighs up a matter partly concerning what is right, pausing briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee or umpire is a person who settles disputes.

clue.text: A motoring organisation to English people

parts.note: RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring body

explanation.surface: A car club belonging to the English.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethnic group or nation of humankind.

clue.text: Appeal for help and love, as is only fair

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: Calling for help and affection is just about acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Middling or mediocre, neither good nor bad.

clue.text: Caught about fifty, but seemed far from pleased

indicators.note: about places the word for caught around the number

parts.note: snared means trapped or caught
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A fielder caught around fifty, but looked unhappy about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Growled angrily, showing displeasure.

clue.text: Clash as a result of industrial action

explanation.definitionFit: To collide or hit, and a walkout by workers.

clue.text: A conservative with no faults whatsoever!

parts.note: the political right is conservative

explanation.surface: A Tory claiming to be perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: Correctly or properly, without error.

clue.text: Tries different ceremonial forms

indicators.note: different asks for the letters of Tries in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone experiments with alternative styles of ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal religious or ceremonial procedures are rituals.

clue.text: An eccentric nature

definitions.meaning: an odd or unusual person is called a real one
one's nature is one's personality or temperament

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an oddball person and someone's essential temperament.

clue.text: A maxim for modern times

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the modern era
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A saying suited to today's world.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional proverb or saying.

clue.text: A man from Armagh

indicators.note: from indicates the letters are made out of Armagh in a different order

explanation.surface: A fellow who comes from the Northern Irish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Armagh is a city and county in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A common male first name.

clue.text: Going through a large number before retiring

indicators.note: before puts the large number ahead of the next piece

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
retiring means departing, leaving

explanation.surface: A big crowd passes through before going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Splitting or cutting a way through something.

clue.text: Family junk

definitions.meaning: a brood of young animals born together

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a brood of young and discarded rubbish.

clue.text: A fan-possibly he daren't show it

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of he daren't can be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A supporter who perhaps is too shy to display allegiance.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower or supporter of a cause or team.
